title: Interpretability of Deep Networks
overview: Interpretability methods help us understand why a network produced a prediction. Gradient-based attributions, attention inspection and probing each give partial, imperfect evidence.

method.title: Saliency
method.body: The gradient of the output with respect to the input shows which input features locally change the score most.

method.title: Integrated gradients
method.body: Accumulates gradients along a path from a baseline to the input, satisfying a completeness axiom.

method.title: Grad-CAM
method.body: Weights convolutional feature maps by their gradients to localize image regions behind a class score.

method.title: Caveats
method.body: Explanations can be unstable or misleading; attention weights are not guaranteed to be faithful explanations, so validate with perturbation tests.

pseudocode:
x.requires_grad = True
score = model(x)[target_class]
score.backward()
saliency = abs(x.grad)
# integrated gradients
ig = (x - base) * mean(grad(model, base + a*(x - base)) for a in alphas)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
w = np.array([2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 0.5])
x = np.array([1.0, 3.0, 5.0, -2.0])
score = lambda v: np.tanh(v @ w)
eps = 1e-5
grad = np.array([(score(x + eps * e) - score(x - eps * e)) / (2 * eps) for e in np.eye(4)])
print("score:", round(float(score(x)), 4))
print("saliency |grad|:", np.round(np.abs(grad), 4))
